The second "Berlin Patient", Timothy Ray Brown, is given a stem cell transplant from a donor carrying the CCR5-Δ32 allele, which cures his HIV/AIDS.
Comet McNaught reaches perihelion and becomes visible from Earth during daylight.
Scientists at the Roslin Institute announce they have genetically engineered chickens to lay eggs containing cancer-fighting proteins.
The Open Handset Alliance launches the Android mobile operating system.
NASA's Dawn spacecraft is launched, beginning its journey to the asteroid belt objects Vesta and Ceres.
Chang'e 1, the first satellite in the Chinese Lunar Exploration Program, is launched from Xichang Satellite Launch Center; on 5 November it enters lunar orbit.
The potentially habitable exoplanet Gliese 581 c is discovered in the constellation Libra.
The New Horizons space probe makes a gravitational slingshot around Jupiter to change its trajectory towards Pluto.
A total solar eclipse takes place, visible in northern Canada, Siberia, Mongolia and northern China.
The Chaitén volcano in Chile enters a new eruptive phase for the first time since around 1640.
The world's first commercial wave farm begins operation off the coast of Portugal.
The first evidence of a volcanic eruption from beneath Antarctica’s most rapidly changing ice sheet is published in the journal Nature Geoscience.
Cyclone Nargis passes through Myanmar, killing more than 138,000 people.
A hybrid human-cow embryo survives a third straight day after being fertilized at Newcastle University, England.
University of Minnesota researchers create a functioning heart in the laboratory by using whole organ decellularization.
Bitcoin is first proposed in a mailing posted to The Cryptography Mailing by a developer under the name of Satoshi Nakamoto.
Researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics and Leibniz University Hanover produce a laser beam of especially high quality.
Biologists create baker's yeast capable of living to 800 in yeast years – a tenfold increase in longevity – without apparent side effects.
28 individual fossils of the giant prehistoric snake T. cerrejonensis are discovered in the coal mines of Cerrejón, La Guajira, Colombia.
Omid, Iran's first domestically built satellite, is successfully launched from Semnan Space Center into low Earth orbit; it re-enters the atmosphere on 25 April.
Iranian researches found that drinking hot tea causes oesophageal cancer.
Iranian scientists find that the way in which traditional timber-framed constructions are built makes them earthquake-resistant.
The first animal from an extinct species to be recreated by cloning, a Pyrenean Ibex, is born alive, but dies seven minutes later due to physical defects in its lungs.
Paleontologists announce the discovery of Darwinius masillae, an evolutionary "missing link" with features similar to lemurs, monkeys, and humans.
The Bitcoin cryptocurrency network is created when the developer known as Satoshi Nakamoto mines the genesis block of its blockchain.
European astronomers discover 32 new exoplanets.
24 May – STS-125, the last Space Shuttle mission to service the Hubble Space Telescope, takes place.
Comet Lulin, a non-periodic comet, makes its closest approach to Earth, peaking in brightness between magnitude +4 and magnitude +6.
Iranian researchers develop a silica-based nano-absorbent to filter harmful heavy metals from waste water.
Scientists decipher the genetic code of the hair of a 4,000-year-old man who was mummified in the permafrost of Greenland.
First (test) Instagram posts made by co-developers Mike Krieger and Kevin Systrom in San Francisco; the service launches publicly on October 6.
Iranian chemists developed a safe way to create nuclear energy with laser.

Scientists conducting the Neanderthal genome project at the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology describe a draft sequence of the Neanderthal (Homo neanderthalensis) genome in the journal Science.
SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft becomes the first commercial spacecraft ever to be successfully retrieved from orbit.
Scientists announce that they are on the verge of creating pills that target specific genes in the human genome to increase longevity.
Japanese scientists announce that they have created working retinas from mouse stem cells.
Researchers in Australia announce that sharks are colorblind, after examining the eyes of 17 separate shark species.
A team of Chinese physicists successfully entangles eight photons simultaneously and observes them in action; the previous record was six.
India's Minister of Health, Ghulam Nabi Azad, reports that the country has almost entirely eradicated polio through a vaccination program which immunises over 170 million children every year.
Swiss researchers discover a gene in wasps that allow them to reproduce asexually.
A study conducted at the Innsbruck Medical University in Austria reveals that stainless steel or titanium tongue piercings harbor more bacteria than plastic piercings.
Israeli engineers have built an artificial device capable of detecting cancers of the head and neck by analysing breath.
South Korean researchers begin the development of microscopic robots capable of entering human blood vessels to treat illnesses.
Six men emerge from the 520-day MARS-500 isolation experiment, which aimed to simulate a human mission to Mars.
Cuban medical authorities release CimaVax-EGF, the first therapeutic vaccine for lung cancer.
A Norwegian liquid natural gas tanker becomes the first ship of its size to attempt a winter crossing of the Arctic.
The Dark Energy Survey's high-resolution camera begins operation in Chile, surveying distant galaxies for evidence of the action of dark energy.
A Belgian team develops a curved LCD contact lens display.
Iran claims to have developed antivirus software capable of defending against the powerful Flame cyberweapon, which has infected computer networks across the Middle East.
After studying 40 years of medical records, Swedish scientists state that those with Huntington's disease are around 50% less likely to develop cancer than those without the disease.
In a breakthrough for adult stem cell therapy, Israeli scientists grow healthy heart muscle cells from the skin cells of patients.
An international team of researchers reports that a new, drug-resistant strain of malaria has emerged on the Thai–Cambodian border, potentially threatening global efforts to contain the disease.
The United Kingdom reports that it is considering the installation of undersea power cables to allow its National Grid to draw clean energy from Iceland's volcanoes.
The solar-powered Solar Impulse aircraft lands in Morocco after a 19-hour flight from Spain, marking the first intercontinental flight of a purely solar-powered aircraft.
Anthropologists in northern Kenya unearth fossils of a previously unconfirmed species of human that lived approximately 2 million years ago.
French glaciologists release a report stating that the glaciers of the Andes are melting at an unprecedented rate.

A team of chemists and physicists from Japan's Yokohama National University produce a material that can be developed into mixed, conductive 3D formations, enabling scientists to create customized brain electrodes.
A 10-ton meteoroid impacts in Chelyabinsk, Russia, producing a powerful shockwave and injuring over 1,000 people.
The first graphene-based circuits to break the gigahertz barrier are created by researchers in the US and Italy.
Australia experiences its hottest day on record, with nationwide average temperatures exceeding 40°C amid one of the most intense bushfire seasons in the country's history.
China is reported to be experiencing a rapid growth in the use of industrial robots, with robot installations increasing at over 10 percent a year.
Britain's first hand transplantation operation is successfully conducted.
Scientists report the results of the oldest human DNA found.
India launches its first Mars probe, Mangalyaan.
The Atacama Large Millimeter Array, at the time the world's most powerful radio telescope, becomes fully operational in northern Chile.

NASA reports Voyager 1, the farthest spacecraft from Earth, experienced a new third "tsunami wave", generated from activity (coronal mass ejections) on the sun, further confirming that the probe is in interstellar space.
Indonesia now has greater rates of deforestation than Brazil, despite its forests being a quarter the size of the Amazon rainforest.
Astronomers have discovered the first evidence of water ice clouds on an object outside of the Solar System.
Scientists in Peru release photographs of a live Cuscomys oblativus (the Machu Picchu arboreal chinchilla rat), which has previously thought to have been extinct.
A partial solar eclipse occurs across most of North America.
President Obama recommends the FCC reclassify broadband Internet service as a telecommunications service in order to preserve net neutrality.
NASA reports that evidence for a large underground ocean of liquid water on Enceladus, moon of planet Saturn, has been found by the Cassini.
Half of all stars may be found in the space between galaxies, according to a new study.
Nautilus Minerals has finalised an agreement with Papua New Guinea over the first deep sea mining operations.
A critical bug (named "Heartbleed") in OpenSSL is estimated to have left 17% of the Internet's secure web servers vulnerable to data theft.
Researchers in China publish results of basic research using CRISPR to edit genes in non-viable human embryos.
Astronomers discover V774104, an object which initially appeared to have a 103 AU distance from the Sun, which would have made it the furthest known object from the sun.
Iranian and Argentinean researchers made a biosensor by using graphene sheets.
Iranian chemists from Ferdowsi University of Mashhad created biodiesel fuel from soya oil to decrease pollutions caused by fossil fuels.
In a world first, researchers from New Zealand have observed mitochondrial DNA moving between cells in mice and triggering cancer growth.
The Sumatran rhinoceros is declared extinct in the wild in Malaysia.
Iranian researchers make magnetic recyclable photo-catalyst to refine dirty water.
Plans are unveiled by Plymouth University for "Mayflower Autonomous Research Ship" (MARS), the world's first full-sized, fully autonomous uncrewed ship to cross the Atlantic Ocean.
NASA administrator, Charlie Bolden, presents the next steps for a human journey to Mars at the Center for American Progress in Washington, D.C.
Archaeologists report finding two lost cities deep in the Honduras jungle, thought to be untouched by humans for at least 600 years.

textFr: Sortie de la version 1.0 du navigateur web Mosaic, créé par Marc Andreessen et Eric Bina.
Intel commercialise ses premières puces Pentium.
La brebis Dolly, premier mammifère cloné à partir d'une cellule adulte, naît en Écosse.
Google est fondé en Californie par Larry Page et Sergey Brin.
Parti des Philippines, le virus informatique ILOVEYOU se propage dans le monde entier.
Le télescope spatial Hubble détecte du sodium dans l'atmosphère d'une exoplanète, une première.
Microsoft lance le système d'exploitation Windows XP.
Apple lance le lecteur multimédia iTunes.
La navette spatiale Columbia se désintègre au-dessus du Texas, tuant ses sept astronautes.
Le satellite WMAP de la NASA achève la première carte détaillée du fond diffus cosmologique.
Mark Zuckerberg lance « TheFacebook », un réseau social destiné aux étudiants de Harvard.
La première vidéo est mise en ligne sur YouTube.
La planète naine Makémaké est découverte dans la ceinture de Kuiper.
Steve Jobs présente le premier iPhone d'Apple à San Francisco.
La comète McNaught devient visible en plein jour depuis la Terre.
Premières publications de test sur Instagram, par ses créateurs Mike Krieger et Kevin Systrom.
Des scientifiques publient une première ébauche du génome de l'homme de Néandertal.
La capsule Dragon de SpaceX devient le premier vaisseau commercial récupéré après un séjour en orbite.
Un méthanier norvégien est le premier navire de sa taille à tenter une traversée hivernale de l'Arctique.
La caméra du Dark Energy Survey entre en service au Chili pour traquer l'énergie noire.
Une équipe belge met au point une lentille de contact à écran LCD incurvé.
Des scientifiques israéliens cultivent des cellules saines de muscle cardiaque à partir de cellules de peau de patients.
Une souche de paludisme résistante aux médicaments apparaît à la frontière entre la Thaïlande et le Cambodge.
Un météoroïde de 10 tonnes frappe Tcheliabinsk, en Russie, et blesse plus de 1 000 personnes.
Des chercheurs américains et italiens créent les premiers circuits en graphène à dépasser le gigahertz.
Des chercheurs chinois publient des résultats sur l'édition génétique par CRISPR d'embryons humains non viables.
Des chimistes iraniens créent du biodiesel à partir d'huile de soja pour réduire la pollution.
Des chercheurs néo-zélandais observent de l'ADN mitochondrial passer d'une cellule à l'autre chez la souris et déclencher un cancer.
Le rhinocéros de Sumatra est déclaré éteint à l'état sauvage en Malaisie.
